newsitem.title: BULGARIA: BULGARIA SEASIDE RESORTS SAID SAFE FROM LANDSLIDES.
newsitem.headline: BULGARIA SEASIDE RESORTS SAID SAFE FROM LANDSLIDES.

text.p: Bulgaria's Black Sea holiday resorts have not suffered from recent coastal landslides and are ready to welcome foreign tourists this summer, Tourism Committee chairman Roumen Draganov said on Wednesday.
"Landslides which appear to be next to the resorts of Golden Sands, Albena and Elenite (north of Bourgas), are not threatening the tourist season of these complexes," Draganov told a news conference.
The Golden Sands, Albena and Elenite resorts are expecting a total of 1.2 million tourists this summer, mainly from Britain, Germany, Russia, and Scandinavia, officials said.
There were two landslides last week above and below two main roads along the coast linking the port of Varna with Golden Sands and Albena.
"There are three other roads linking Varna and the airport with Golden Sands and Albena," Draganov said.

Varna regional governor Dobrin Mitev told Reuters no bookings had been cancelled. He said the Golden Sands resort, which is between two landslides, did not lie on susceptible soil and had never had such problems.
More than 20 hectares (50 acres) of a holiday villa zone near Varna had dropped towards the sea. The holiday homes were mostly unoccupied and there were no casualties, Mitev said.

Geologists have been warning of landslides in the area for 50 years and only small buildings were supposed to be permitted there, local media said. But big, multi-storey houses had been built recently in breach of regulations, officials said.
"The cause for the landslides is heavy rain, large buildups of underground water, illegal buildings which are heavy for such a soil, and a lack of drainage," Mitev said.

Spring floods have covered hundreds of hectares of arable land in eastern Bulgaria and reservoirs are being closely monitored as some are nearing critical levels and could overflow, a civil defence official said.
